comparison: Both evaluate claims C4, C42, C43, C44 regarding oocyte volume increase and developmental progression. OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED by imaging and quantitative data. Peer review also finds them SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 noting solid conclusions and no challenges to the developmental staging observations.

Both evaluate claims C7, C52-C56 regarding granulosa cell loss via lineage tracing. OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED with 94% loss statistically validated. Peer review rates them UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 critiquing that cell loss should be assessed with cell death markers rather than loss of labeled cells due to variable labeling efficiency.

Both evaluate claims C8, C62-C66 regarding Cyp17a1 lineage tracing and theca/interstitial cell characterization. OpenEval finds the claims SUPPORTED by lineage tracing, electron microscopy, and 3D reconstruction. Peer review also finds them SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 accepting the findings while requesting higher magnification images.

Both evaluate claim C77 regarding absence of Fshr expression. OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED by expression data, consistent with gonadotropin-independent development. Peer review also finds it SUPPORTED without challenge from any reviewer.

Both evaluate claims C107-C108 regarding transient phenotype in genetic model. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED but notes limitations due to transient nature. Peer review also finds them SUPPORTED as secondary observations not challenged by reviewers.

Both evaluate claims C5, C6, C45-C51 regarding oocyte loss and atresia. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by quantitative data, electron microscopy, and validation in multiple strains. Peer review rates them UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 requesting cell death markers in lineage-traced ovaries rather than relying on morphological observations alone.

Both evaluate claims C11-C13, C30-C31, C57-C61 regarding boundary follicles and preferential activation. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by quantitative lineage tracing showing 70% of secondary follicles labeled. Peer review rates them UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting that labeled boundary follicles were previously observed (Zhang et al. 2013) and that scRNA-seq on lineage-traced ovaries would be more definitive. Reviewer 1 questions whether special gene expression patterns distinguish boundary follicles.

Both evaluate background claims C20-C25, C27-C29 from literature. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer review also finds them SUPPORTED, accepting this context without challenge.

Both evaluate claims C9, C10, C69, C70, C74-C76 regarding steroidogenic cell characterization and gene expression. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by electron microscopy, scRNA-seq, and temporal analysis. Peer review also finds them SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging key gene identification and requesting better visualization of cell number changes.

Both evaluate claims C15, C93-C94, C117-C123 regarding differential gene expression between wave 1 and wave 2 follicles. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by scRNA-seq data showing quantified expression ratios. Peer review rates them UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 stating the central question should be investigated more deeply with validation on lineage-traced ovaries (e.g., Wnt4 staining) across all developmental stages.

Both evaluate claims C14, C32, C53, C82-C83 regarding boundary follicles' role in early fertility. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED, noting the inference is logically derived from quantitative data. Peer review rates them UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 explicitly stating the study does not directly assess fertility outcomes and should refrain from drawing conclusions about fertility potential.

Both evaluate literature-based and speculative claims C85-C90, C95, C97, C104-C106, C110-C113, C115-C116. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED as appropriately cited comparative and clinical context. Peer review rates overlapping claims (including C34, C79, C84-C92, C95-C106, C111-C116) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are largely speculative or interpretive discussion claims that exceed the data, particularly regarding fertility conclusions.

Both evaluate claims C67-C68, C72-C73 regarding scRNA-seq clustering and trajectory analysis identifying two developmental paths. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by standard scRNA-seq methods. Peer review also finds them SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 noting high-quality results and requesting better visualization, while Reviewer 3's critique about not using lineage-traced ovaries is noted as a missed opportunity rather than challenging data quality.

Both evaluate claims C71, C124-C126 regarding remodeling follicles and pathway analysis. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by scRNA-seq data and Metascape analysis showing fourfold increase in endothelial/blood cells. Peer review also finds related claims SUPPORTED (C67-C73, C124-C126), accepting the scRNA-seq profiling quality.

Both evaluate claims C39-C41 regarding medulla-cortex boundary criteria for wave 1 follicle identification. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by whole-mount imaging and follicle counting with Imaris. Peer review rates them UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 explicitly critiquing the boundary as 'somewhat arbitrary' and stating that FOXL2-lineage-traced ovaries provide a more reliable method. The editor also notes justification for criteria would benefit from further explanation.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1, C2, C16, C17, C39-C41 regarding wave 1 follicle quantification and identification. Peer review R14 evaluates overlapping background claims C1, C2, C16-C19, C26 as SUPPORTED established knowledge. The peer review accepts the foundational context but does not specifically address the quantification methodology that OpenEval evaluates.

OpenEval evaluates claims C15, C93-C94, C117-C123 regarding differential gene expression between waves. Peer review R13 evaluates subset C117-C119 as SUPPORTED gene expression patterns from scRNA-seq without challenge. However, peer review R9 rates the broader set including C15, C93-C94, C120-C123 as UNCERTAIN, requesting deeper investigation with validation.

Both evaluate speculative mechanistic claims. OpenEval evaluates C84, C91, C96, C99, C101, C114 as UNCERTAIN, noting they are reasonable hypotheses lacking direct experimental validation. Peer review evaluates a much broader set (C34, C79, C84-C92, C95-C106, C111-C116) as UNCERTAIN, stating these discussion claims are largely speculative and exceed the data, particularly regarding fertility conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates claims C18-C29 as SUPPORTED background literature. Peer review R14 evaluates subset C1, C2, C16-C19, C26 as SUPPORTED established knowledge, while R15 evaluates C20-C25, C27-C29 as SUPPORTED. Both agree these foundational claims are appropriately cited and accepted.

OpenEval evaluates claims C92, C98, C100, C102-C103 regarding boundary follicle characterization and intrinsic differences as SUPPORTED by correspondence to previous studies and scRNA-seq data. Peer review R16 includes these claims in a broader UNCERTAIN evaluation, treating them as speculative interpretive claims in the discussion that are not directly tested.

OpenEval evaluates claims C34, C80-C81 regarding reinterpretation of previous findings as SUPPORTED, noting the inference is logically supported by boundary follicle data. Peer review R7 evaluates overlapping claims C30-C32, C80-C81 as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 noting that labeled boundary follicles were previously observed and questioning the novelty.

OpenEval evaluates claim C109 regarding temporal correlation with peri-puberty as SUPPORTED by lineage tracing and scRNA-seq showing peak at 4-5 weeks. Peer review R6 evaluates overlapping claims including C109-C110 as SUPPORTED, accepting the steroidogenic findings and temporal patterns.

OpenEval evaluates claims C78-C79 regarding agreement with earlier studies on oocyte loss and steroidogenic role as SUPPORTED. Peer review R3 evaluates C78 along with C5, C6, C45-C51 as UNCERTAIN, requesting cell death markers in lineage-traced ovaries to demonstrate the mechanistic claims about atresia.

OpenEval evaluates claims C9, C10, C69, C70, C74-C76 regarding steroidogenic characterization. Peer review R10 evaluates overlapping claim C69 along with C67-C68, C71-C73, C124-C126 as SUPPORTED scRNA-seq findings. Both accept the quality of the molecular characterization data.

OpenEval evaluates claim C109 regarding temporal correlation of theca cell expansion with peri-puberty as SUPPORTED by lineage tracing and scRNA-seq data. While peer review R6 touches on C109, no peer review result specifically focuses on this temporal correlation claim as a primary evaluation target.

OpenEval evaluates claims C34, C80-C81 as SUPPORTED reinterpretation based on boundary follicle discovery. Peer review R16 includes C34 in a broad set of UNCERTAIN speculative discussion claims. The peer review treats the reinterpretation as exceeding the data rather than as logically supported inference.

OpenEval evaluates claims C78-C79 as SUPPORTED agreement with earlier studies. Peer review R16 includes C79 in a broad set of UNCERTAIN speculative discussion claims that exceed the data. The evaluations diverge on whether these synthesis claims are appropriately supported.

OpenEval evaluates claims C92, C98, C100, C102-C103 regarding boundary follicle characterization and intrinsic differences as SUPPORTED by correspondence to previous studies and differential gene expression. While peer review R16 includes some of these claims, no peer review result specifically focuses on the intrinsic vs. extrinsic factor question as a primary evaluation.
